title: API Security Fundamentals '25
description:
# API Security Fundamentals '25  

**Issued by:** APIsec University  
**Level:** Foundational  
**Duration:** 2 Hours  
**Skill Area:** API Security  

Successfully completed the **API Security Fundamentals '25** course, focused on understanding and mitigating core threats targeting modern APIs.

This course explored real-world API breaches and analyzed how attackers exploit exposed endpoints, business logic flaws, and misconfigurations. A deep dive into the **OWASP API Security Top 10** highlighted critical risks such as broken object-level authorization (BOLA), excessive data exposure, injection vulnerabilities, and improper asset management.

The program also introduced the **Three Pillars of API Security**:
- **Governance** – Establishing policies, standards, and secure API design practices  
- **Testing** – Continuous security validation through automated and manual testing  
- **Monitoring** – Ongoing visibility, logging, and threat detection  

Additional modules covered the broader application security technology landscape and provided strategic guidance for building secure API programs across development and security teams.

**Earning Criteria:**
- Completed all training modules (2 hours)  
- Passed all module quizzes  
- Successfully cleared the final assessment  

This certification reinforces a strong foundational understanding of API attack surfaces, compliance considerations, and best practices necessary to protect sensitive data and application logic in modern, API-driven architectures.

title: API Penetration Testing
description:
# API Penetration Testing  

**Issued by:** APIsec University  
**Duration:** 12 Hours  
**Focus Area:** Offensive API Security & Vulnerability Assessment  

Successfully completed the **API Penetration Testing** course, a hands-on program centered on identifying and exploiting security weaknesses in modern APIs.

This course emphasized practical testing methodologies and real-world attack simulations against API endpoints. It covered structured approaches to:

- **API Reconnaissance** – Mapping endpoints, identifying hidden routes, and analyzing API documentation leaks  
- **Scanning & Enumeration** – Discovering misconfigurations and exposed functionality  
- **JWT Auditing** – Analyzing JSON Web Tokens for weak signing algorithms, key mismanagement, and privilege escalation vectors  
- **Authentication & Authorization Attacks** – Testing for broken object-level authorization (BOLA), broken function-level authorization (BFLA), and access control bypasses  
- **Common API Exploits** – Injection flaws, mass assignment vulnerabilities, and server-side request forgery (SSRF)  

The training reinforced a structured penetration testing workflow tailored specifically to APIs, combining manual techniques with automated tools to uncover logic flaws and data exposure risks.

Completion of this course demonstrates practical capability in offensive API security testing and a deeper understanding of how modern API ecosystems can be attacked—and secured.

title: OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023 Edition)
description:
Completed a focused training program covering the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023), with an in-depth exploration of the most critical security risks affecting modern APIs. The course provided practical insights into how these vulnerabilities are exploited and how to effectively mitigate them.

Key Learning Areas:

API1: Broken Object Level Authorization (BOLA): Identified risks of unauthorized data access
API2: Broken Authentication: Analyzed weaknesses in authentication mechanisms
API3: Broken Object Property Level Authorization: Explored excessive data exposure issues
API4: Unrestricted Resource Consumption: Understood DoS and rate-limiting weaknesses
API5: Broken Function Level Authorization (BFLA): Tested privilege escalation scenarios
API6: Unrestricted Access to Sensitive Business Flows: Examined abuse of business logic
API7: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF): Identified server-side exploitation vectors
API8: Security Misconfiguration: Detected improper configurations and defaults
API9: Improper Inventory Management: Assessed shadow and deprecated APIs
API10: Unsafe Consumption of APIs: Evaluated risks from third-party integrations

Outcome:
Developed a strong understanding of API-specific attack surfaces and defensive strategies, enabling effective identification and mitigation of common API vulnerabilities in real-world environments.

Skills:
API Security, OWASP Top 10, Application Security, Authorization Testing, Risk Assessment, Secure API Design

title: Certified API Security Analyst (CASA)
description:
Certified API Security Analyst (CASA)

The Certified API Security Analyst (CASA) certification demonstrates practical and theoretical expertise in securing modern APIs against real-world threats.

This certification validates a strong understanding of:

The OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023)
Common API vulnerabilities and attack patterns
Secure API design and implementation practices
Authentication and authorization mechanisms (OAuth 2.0, JWT, tokens)
API security testing and risk identification
Key Competencies
Identifying and exploiting API vulnerabilities such as BOLA, BFLA, BOPLA, SSRF, and Broken Authentication
Understanding token-based security, scopes, and claims
Securing API infrastructure including CORS, rate limiting, error handling, and server hardening
Evaluating and improving API documentation from a security perspective
Applying secure coding and defensive design principles
Certification Requirements
Successfully completed a 100-question exam
Covered API risks, threats, and best practices
Achieved 80%+ score
Why it matters

APIs expose critical business logic and sensitive data. This certification demonstrates the ability to:

Assess API security posture
Perform API penetration testing
Recommend and implement secure API architectures
